script: I started Ozempic, my best friend exposed a nightmare—now I am terrified.. I started Ozempic at the beginning of June, weighing a solid 368 lbs. I am a self‑proclaimed body‑loving advocate, but I am tired of feeling like a human wreck. So I kept the medication under wraps, just the online doctor and me. The first thing the doctor did was a blood test—spoiler: I am pre‑diabetic. My whole life's been overweight, no diabetes, but family history says otherwise. So now I am not just dropping weight; I am also preventing a full‑blown type‑2 diabetes. (Micro‑hook: I am not just losing pounds, I am dodging a future nightmare.) Fast forward eight weeks. I am down almost ten pounds, binge‑eating is a thing of the past, I hit the pool three times a week, and I am hitting protein and fiber goals. My sugar intake is through the roof—like, literally, it's gone down dramatically. The pre‑diabetes results forced me to shift from a "fat‑loss diet" mindset, which would trigger my binge‑eating disorder, to a real lifestyle change because, honestly, I don't want to be diabetic. (Stakes: my health, my mental space, my confidence.) Then my bestie drops a post in our group chat saying Ozempic is terrible, that the side effects are awful, and that people should avoid it. Another friend chimes in, agreeing. Meanwhile, I am pumping this stuff in, seeing real results, and feeling more energized than ever. (Micro‑hook: My friends are talking about it like it's a bad thing, but I am living the good thing.) I know I'd love to share this journey with my friends and family. But the thought that they'll smile, then gossip behind my back? The audacity, right? I hate that my health is a mental weight, that if I stay fat people worry about me, and if I try to help myself, they worry about me too. I am stuck in this endless loop. I just can't win.
